wiki_text: Egypt's LNG balance inverted in 2024-2025. Declining domestic gas output (notably falling Zohr-field production and reduced Israeli pipeline supply, including a disruption when Israel curtailed Leviathan flows) drove a widening domestic deficit, collapsing the country's exportable surplus from its export terminals (Idku/ELNG and Damietta/SEGAS) and turning Egypt into a substantial net LNG importer. LNG imports rose ~188% year-on-year over the first 11 months of 2025 (≈7.8 Mt / ~10 bcm year-to-date), and full-year 2025 imports reached a record (reported ≈8.9 Mt). The U.S. EIA documents the same trajectory: a growing natural-gas deficit forcing Egypt to ramp up LNG imports. To absorb the imports through peak summer power demand, EGAS rapidly chartered and positioned multiple FSRUs across Ain Sokhna (Sonker berth), the adjacent Port of Sumed, and Damietta. Export terminals kept running only intermittently, loading occasional opportunistic cargoes when feedgas allowed (see per-terminal notes).

Although the two-train Idku (ELNG) plant remained physically operational, exports became sporadic as feedgas was prioritized for domestic power. Feedgas to ELNG resumed around March 2025; ELNG then loaded a rare export cargo in September 2025 (reported as its first cargo in months), and further cargoes loaded in January 2026 (a cargo to Canada on 11 January and to Türkiye on 26 January). The government authorized Shell and Petronas to export up to two cargoes per month over a multi-month window (with a broader plan permitting a minimum number of cargoes annually through 2029), but tightening domestic supply forced exports to be suspended again by around March 2026. The pattern is stop-start export operation governed by feedgas availability rather than any plant lifecycle change.

topic: Energos Winter charter and Brazil provenance
wiki_text: The Energos Winter (138,250 m3 FSRU, owned by Energos Infrastructure, the Apollo-managed vehicle) was placed at EGAS's Damietta import terminal under a 5-year regasification service agreement signed with New Fortress Energy in July 2025; it received its first LNG cargo at Damietta in October 2025 (delivered from Cheniere's Sabine Pass). It is the second NFE/Energos FSRU in Egypt, joining the Energos Eskimo. The vessel was relocated FROM Brazil: it had served Petrobras's Terminal Gas Sul (TGS) in Santa Catarina and was handed to New Fortress Energy in December 2023 (an accelerated redeployment after Petrobras chartered the Excelerate Sequoia) before its move to Egypt. ASC Maritime provided conversion/commissioning support (June-October 2025) for Damietta operation. This is a cross-project FSRU sync/reassignment touchpoint.

topic: Höegh Galleon interim charter and pending Australia move; Gandria replacement
wiki_text: The Höegh Galleon (170,000 m3 FSRU, owned/operated by Höegh Evi, formerly Höegh LNG) was deployed to Egypt's Gulf of Suez on an interim charter agreed by Höegh LNG, Australian Industrial Energy (AIE) and EGAS, operating from around June/July 2024. It is to remain in Egypt up to roughly an additional year, after which Höegh Evi plans to relocate it to AIE's Port Kembla LNG import terminal in Australia (expected 2027, ~15-year deployment) - a cross-project FSRU reassignment to watch. To backfill the Sumed berth, EGAS signed a 10-year time charter (announced May 2025) for the Höegh Gandria (an ex-LNG carrier purchased Feb 2023, undergoing FSRU conversion), with deployment to the Port of Sumed in Q4 2026 and up to ~1,000 mmscf/d of peak regasification.

topic: Energos Eskimo 10-year charter, relocated from Jordan
wiki_text: The Energos Eskimo (160,663 m3 FSRU, ex-Golar Eskimo, built 2014, owned by Energos Infrastructure/Apollo) operates at the Port of Sumed under a 10-year charter EGAS signed with New Fortress Energy (announced December 2024). The vessel was relocated to Egypt from Jordan, where it had served the Aqaba (Sheikh Sabah Al-Ahmad Port) regasification terminal since 2015; it arrived at Sumed around June 2025 for upgrades and became operational about July 2025. Cross-project FSRU reassignment touchpoint (Jordan -> Egypt).
